project.name: FTA – Forensic Triage for Android
project.purpose: Defensive toolkit to check one's own Android phone for stalkerware, spyware, malware, tampering and privacy abuse; complements signature scanners such as Malwarebytes.
audience: phone owners investigating their own device
principles: Nothing leaves the device/computer without explicit user action; VirusTotal receives hashes/domains only, uploads need confirmation
Honest coverage: every report states its blind spots
No third-party dependencies (no AndroidX, no pip packages)

sentinel.name: DroidSentinel
sentinel.purpose: Always-on monitor with dashboard (privacy risk, security risk, suspicious activity, unknown binaries, malware detected).
features: Integrity baseline per package: APK changed without update, signer change, downgrade, installer change, icon hidden
Instant package broadcasts + 15 min rescans; notifications for new HIGH/CRITICAL findings
DNS-only local VPN: per-app DNS log with IOC / DGA / dynamic DNS / tunnel / Telegram-bot / tracker flags
Per-app traffic via NetworkStatsManager; uploads while screen off; hidden apps uploading
Pluggable risk engine (AppRules/DeviceRules): accessibility, admin, notification listener, IME, overlay, SMS, StrandHogg task affinity, masquerading, platform key, packers
VirusTotal hash lookups (rate limited, cached); file upload only after two-step confirmation
Stalkerware IOC feed download/import; JSON report export; signature-protected report provider for the Collector

collector.name: DroidCollector
collector.purpose: Consent-gated export of logs, dumpsys, settings, CA certs, usage/network history, app inventory, APKs and the Sentinel report into one hashed zip. No INTERNET permission.
features: Capability detection: READ_LOGS / DUMP (adb grants), usage access, Sentinel report
Every zip entry hashed into manifest.json with its source command
Hash policy: user + updated system APKs by default, all system APKs on request

maturity.compiled: GitHub Actions run 39624022772: ./gradlew test assembleRelease succeeded (AGP 8.5.2, compileSdk 34), APK artifact produced; also type-checked locally with tools/kotlin_check.sh
maturity.tested: shares core unit tests; no collector-specific tests
maturity.notes: Output layout is exercised indirectly by droidtriage tests (synthetic evidence in the same layout).

droidtriage.name: droidtriage
droidtriage.purpose: Offline deep analysis of collector/adb evidence with HTML/JSON/CSV reports.
features: Analyser registry: inventory, apk, virustotal, device, dumpsys, packages, logcat, network
Pure-python APK static analysis: binary manifest, DEX strings, v1/v2/v3 signer certs, payloads, packers, trackers, hosts
dumpsys parsing: roles, device owner, appops background use, jobs/alarms persistence, dropbox crashes, ADB keys, settings history
Logcat rules with keyword pre-filter; timeline with normalised timestamps
IOC feeds: stalkerware-indicators YAML, MVT STIX2, text lists
Baseline diff, standalone APK command, IOC check, VirusTotal commands, synthetic sample generator

maturity.tested: stdlib unittest suite (unit + end-to-end CLI), Python 3.9 and 3.13; binary parsers validated on a real APK (PCAPdroid 1.7.2)
maturity.notes: Never run on evidence from a real phone; dumpsys regexes follow AOSP formats and may need tuning per vendor/version.

adb_collect.name: adb_collect.sh
adb_collect.purpose: Same evidence layout collected over adb (shell user: full dumpsys/logcat), optional bugreport for MVT.

setup.name: setup.sh + tools/build.sh
setup.purpose: Deterministic toolchain bootstrap on Linux: detect distro (apt/dnf/pacman/zypper), JDK 17 (distro package or pinned Temurin, rejects JREs), pinned Android SDK (cmdline-tools checksum, platform 34, build-tools 34.0.0), local.properties/.fta-env, keystore, then tests + APKs into dist/ with BUILD_INFO.txt.

maturity.tested: tools/tests/test_setup.py (11 cases via --plan: Debian JRE-only/JDK, 7 distro families, SDK resolution, check exit codes, build.sh Java guard); shellcheck clean
maturity.real_runs: Ubuntu 24.04: apt install of openjdk-17-jdk-headless and pinned Temurin download+checksum verified; Android SDK download not reachable from the dev sandbox -> covered by the CI setup-linux matrix (debian:12, ubuntu:24.04, fedora:41, archlinux)
maturity.notes: x86_64 only (Google's Linux build-tools); Alpine unsupported.

kotlin_check.name: kotlin_check.sh
kotlin_check.purpose: Compile Android Kotlin sources and run JVM unit tests without the Android SDK (Robolectric android-all jar).

maturity.tested: used for every Kotlin change in this repo

history.summary: Initial build: DroidSentinel, DroidCollector, droidtriage, adb_collect.sh, GUIDE, RISK_MATRIX, sample report. Analyzer tested on synthetic evidence + one real APK; Kotlin type-checked against android-all.

Analyzer: analyser registry, subcommand CLI, logcat pre-filter (2.7x faster), parallel APK analysis, timestamp normalisation, fixed file-handle leak, 51 tests incl. end-to-end and parity. Android: pluggable rule engine, DB indexes (DNS first-seen query was a full scan per packet), HashPolicy (first scan no longer hashes all system APKs), JVM unit tests, kotlin_check harness. Skills, CLAUDE.md, project index, CI with tests.
First GitHub Actions run green: Python 3.9/3.13 suites, real-APK parser tests, index check, Android unit tests and release APK build.

setup.sh + tools/build.sh: distro detection, JDK 17 resolution (JRE-only installs detected), pinned Android SDK with checksum, local.properties/.fta-env, dist/ with SHA256SUMS + BUILD_INFO; Gradle wrapper checksum; CI builds from scratch on 4 distributions. Fixed a pipefail+grep -q false negative found by a real apt run.

known_limitations: Android apps build in CI (AGP) and pass JVM unit tests, but have never run on a device: runtime permissions, foreground-service/VPN behaviour and OEM battery killers are unverified
DNS monitor is bypassed by DoH/hard-coded resolvers and Strict Private DNS; NetworkStats attribution lags minutes
Logcat retention is short; dumpsys formats vary by Android version/OEM
No detection of kernel/firmware implants, zero-click exploits without traces, cloud-account or carrier-side attacks
Malwarebytes column of RISK_MATRIX is based on public documentation, not tested
Python 3.9 is the floor; Windows is untested for adb_collect.sh (use WSL/Git Bash)
Toolchain bootstrap targets x86_64 Linux (Google ships Linux build-tools for x86_64 only); macOS/Windows: use Android Studio or CI
roadmap: First real-device validation of both apps; fix issues found
Instrumented/Robolectric tests for Store, Scanner diff and Collector layout
Vendor-specific dumpsys parser fixtures (Samsung, Xiaomi) from real collections
Optional MVT interoperability (export findings as STIX2 / read MVT JSON)
Localised UI strings (currently English, built in code)

conventions.finding_id: family.rule, lowercase, stable; dev.* device-level; log.* logcat; apk.* static analysis
conventions.severity: CRITICAL confirmed compromise; HIGH abusable access or tampering; MEDIUM suspicious; LOW hygiene; INFO context
conventions.scores: security = sum(weights of SECURITY+MALWARE findings) capped 100 with CRITICAL 40 / HIGH 15 / MEDIUM 5 / LOW 1; privacy = 0.6*max + 0.4*avg(top10 user-app permission scores)
conventions.tests: plain-text/JSON fixtures; real APK via DROIDTRIAGE_TEST_APK; no fabricated binaries
